Both windows use [CloudSandboxSessionContribution](../../../../workbench/contrib/chat/browser/remoteAgentHost/cloudSandboxSessionContribution.ts) for sandbox discovery, connection-on-open, and offline history. Each supplies its own session-list adapter. Discovery remains account-wide; the Editor adapter scopes its list to the workspace's GitHub repositories, or all projects in an empty window, and groups its filters under Cloud. Repository scope applies to cached and connected sessions without changing their routing; opening one preserves its host and session identity and does not provision a replacement. Both windows create sandboxes through the shared contribution's provisioning path, which seeds the created task like a discovered one before connecting. The Editor offers a single `cloud-sandbox` creation target in the harness picker with a repository option group derived from the workspace's GitHub repositories plus "No Repository"; discovered environment providers stay registered for existing conversations but remain excluded from the picker and automatic new-chat selection. On the first send, the Editor provisions the sandbox, reports progress through a cancellable notification, and returns the item under the environment's own session type so the untitled draft rebinds to it. A selected repository resolves the new session's working directory to its GitHub URL for session preparation; "No Repository" explicitly leaves the working directory to the host rather than substituting a local workspace folder.

+Sandbox session discovery is window-owned and does not establish host connections. A full refresh reconciles absent disconnected environments; incremental refreshes retain absent entries and reconcile only explicitly removed or replaced tasks. Both preserve connected and provisioning environments. Feed task reads do not wait for inventory scans; completing scans preserve newer task updates and removals from those reads. Failed or cancelled scans must not advance incremental discovery progress.

+The shared sandbox contribution owns an optional, account-scoped Mission Control task feed while the sandbox feature is enabled. `chat.agentHost.cloudSandbox.sessionFeed.enabled` permits a connection attempt or selects polling only; GitHub's server-side feature flag controls feed availability. Changing the setting closes or starts the subscription without recreating session providers or disconnecting sandbox hosts. It subscribes before the initial task read, treats task-change notifications as invalidations of the named tasks rather than authoritative metadata, and refreshes the inventory after reconnecting. The task APIs remain authoritative, with a slow safety poll for missed notifications and normal discovery polling when the feed is unavailable. Unavailable or failed connection attempts are recorded at debug level without automatic retries for that subscription lifetime. An established socket may reconnect once after disconnection; a failed reconnect or renewal likewise falls back to polling. Reloading the window, changing accounts, or toggling feed or sandbox enablement permits another probe. Account changes, feature disablement, and window disposal close the subscription without changing sandbox host connection ownership.

Cloud sandbox environments are automatically trusted like Codespaces. The sandbox contribution registers each environment's exact filesystem scheme and authority with workspace trust before publishing its provider, including cached offline providers, and releases that registration when the environment is removed. Registrations do not persist user-granted folder trust or trust other authorities. The connection customization also exempts sandbox message sending from the current window's workspace-trust gate.
